{{< section_nav >}}

Geoscientific knowledge and remote-sensing data are connected. Intelligent remote-sensing analysis should use relationships among datasets to provide richer information and perspectives. Combining the mechanisms of geoscientific processes with collaborative cognitive models for objects in high-resolution imagery, constrained by geoscientific knowledge, can improve the accuracy and efficiency of object recognition in large remote-sensing datasets.

### 1. Collaborative object recognition in high-resolution imagery constrained by geoscientific knowledge

#### (1) Hierarchical deep learning for urban buildings, enabling building extraction across large areas
![Hierarchical deep-learning extraction of urban buildings](image.png)


#### (2) A deep-learning framework for all types of photovoltaic installations in large-scale, ultra-high-resolution imagery, enabling the first detailed nationwide mapping of centralized and distributed photovoltaics in China at 0.3 m resolution
![Nationwide deep-learning extraction of centralized and distributed photovoltaics at 0.3 m resolution](image-1.png)


#### (3) The Hierarchical Pyramid Refined U-Net (HPR-UNet) semantic segmentation model, producing the first nationwide 2 m multi-type marine aquaculture product covering raft aquaculture, cages, and deep-water circular cages
![Nationwide multi-type marine aquaculture mapping with HPR-UNet](image-2.png)


#### (4) Object recognition in high-resolution imagery of rare-earth mining areas constrained by vegetation indices, enabling fast and accurate extraction of mining-area information
![High-resolution remote-sensing extraction of rare-earth mining areas constrained by vegetation indices](image-3.png)
